title: playing game 2026 09 10
text:
LONDON, Sept 10 (Reuters) - U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is talking a good game with financial markets. "I have asymmetric information. I am the house now," he said this week. "And you can bet against me if you want."
Bessent's comments come after an unusual joint U.S.-Japan ​intervention in the yen over the summer. He maintains that he has information that traders don’t have. In ‌game theory, that’s known as asymmetric information.
When it comes to the Japanese currency, things are going Bessent’s way. It’s rallying ahead of an expected interest rate hike from the Bank of Japan next week. But in the bond market, not so much. Bessent has supersized Treasury buybacks to try and get yields ​down but it’s not working. Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields reached their highest levels since 2023 this week.
Asymmetric information is helpful, but ​in the bond market, size matters too and a $6 billion intervention in a $32 trillion market doesn’t count for ⁠much.
As columnist Jamie McGeever points out, the U.S. bond market is working exactly as it should. The economy is growing, the labour market is ​in good shape, inflation is stubbornly over the Fed’s 2% target and the budget deficit is expected to widen further – and that’s before ​anyone does the maths on U.S. President Donald Trump’s pledge to pay Americans $5,000 each if the Republicans retain control of Congress after November.
Crucially for the bond and oil markets, the Iran war looks set to drag on for months, and that’s going to be bad for inflation. Benchmark oil prices are back above $100 ​a barrel and U.S. diesel prices, a key pressure point for U.S. farmers and businesses, hit record highs.
Researchers at Anthropic are warning

 that there ​is a greater than 10% chance AI “could kill all humans”. The comments have gone viral and shine a light, once again, on the risks around ‌AI. Reuters ⁠is reporting this week that AI agents’ rogue activity is worse than previously thought with agents unleashed by OpenAI using at least 10 more sites for unauthorized communications than previously known. OpenAI is now pushing for mandatory national AI safety requirements.
